A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SiDA research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching experiments and algorithms relocated in v3.

before.justification: v1 reports original SiDA and SiD2A generation results on CIFAR-10, ImageNet 64x64, FFHQ, and AFHQ-v2, including quantitative comparisons and alpha ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains those experiments and adds original ImageNet 512x512 distillation results, model-size comparisons, and a real-data subsampling experiment.

M1.justification: The core shared-discriminator SiDA procedure remains. v3 adds EDM2-specific adaptations: optional learned log-variance loss weighting, modified or disabled forced weight normalization, and a separately weighted discriminator loss (Algorithm 2 and Appendix B.2). Equation (7) also changes the stated generator adversarial term from D to ln D; the PDFs do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: v3 adds label-conditioned ImageNet 512x512 generation, substantially extending the resolution and complexity of the evaluated task. CIFAR-10, ImageNet 64x64, FFHQ 64x64, and AFHQ-v2 64x64 remain covered; relocated face-generation results are retained.

E2.justification: The original benchmark comparator sets remain. v3 adds comparisons with sCT and sCD in Table 4 and a substantially broader high-resolution comparison set in Table 9, including MaskGIT, MAGVIT-v2, MAR, and VAR. These include results attributed to prior work, rather than necessarily new baseline implementations.

E3.justification: New EDM2 experiments cover six model sizes from 125M to 1.5B parameters, with batch size 2048 and learning rate 5e-5. v3 adds FDDINOv2 evaluation and a controlled 5%-versus-100% real-training-data comparison. The documented settings of the retained EDM benchmarks are otherwise preserved.

E4.justification: The existing alpha ablations remain. v3 adds a targeted data-availability test (Figure 7), qualitative comparisons of normalization and learned loss-weighting choices (Appendix B.2), and fixed-noise training-progression visualizations (Figures 8–10). The normalization comparisons lack detailed numerical ablation tables.

E5.justification: v1 already reports results with plus/minus values but does not explain the repetition count. v3 Appendix A explicitly describes ten independent re-evaluations of selected generators. This newly documents evaluation repetition; it does not establish an increase in runs or ten independent training seeds.

E6.justification: Original benchmark values remain unchanged, including v1 Tables 4–5 relocated to v3 Tables 7–8. New ImageNet 512x512 results include SiD2A FIDs of 1.669 for S and 1.366 for XXL (Table 4). Table 10 adds FDDINOv2 results with different rankings: XXL SiD2A scores 44.52 versus 33.09 for the guided teacher. New convergence and subsampling findings are also reported.

T1.justification: Equation (7) substantively revises the mathematical definition of the adversarial generator loss by introducing logarithms. Algorithm 2 additionally formalizes the optional log-variance-weighted objective. The underlying Fisher-divergence and score-identity mathematics remain, without new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: v3 extends the central performance claim from low-resolution EDM distillation to guidance-free, single-step ImageNet 512x512 generation across six EDM2 sizes. It specifically claims that an EDM2-S student can outperform the guided EDM2-XXL teacher and presents adapting SiD to EDM2 as an additional contribution.

C2.justification: The imperfect-teacher motivation remains. v3 adds qualifications about unavoidable approximate-score bias despite alternative stop-gradient interpretations, explicitly discusses iteration overhead, and explains normalization-related backpropagation failures. It also revises the GDD-I feature-leakage discussion and identifies guidance and post-hoc EMA techniques omitted from its EDM2 experiments.

D1.justification: Beyond v1's EDM pseudocode and settings table, v3 supplies EDM2-specific hyperparameters, hardware, timing, and memory measurements (Table 6), model-specific normalization choices, and original/modified MPConv code listings. Appendices A–B also document loss balancing and checkpoint selection. The code-integration statement remains a future promise.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands positioning against EDM2, concurrent sCD, and the high-resolution generative-model landscape. It adds discussion of Luo et al. (2024)'s alternative SiD justification and distinguishes OSGAN's terminology. The account of GDD-I changes from an LPIPS discriminator to Projected-GAN-style VGG16-BN and EfficientNet-lite0 features.

P1.justification: The experimental narrative and appendices are substantially reorganized: setup moves from the main text into Appendix A, algorithms move into an expanded Appendix B, and supplementary results collect in Appendix C. Benchmarking splits into EDM and EDM2 subsections, while the abstract and conclusion are revised around the expanded scope. Much introductory and foundational prose remains.

P2.justification: v3 adds an algorithm schematic, model-size comparison tables, a six-panel convergence figure, a subsampling plot, training snapshots, and high-resolution image galleries. Existing plots are resized and wrapped alongside text; CIFAR and ImageNet convergence panels are regrouped, while FFHQ/AFHQ tables and curves move to the appendix. These are substantial display and layout changes.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens scalability evidence beyond v1's 32x32 and 64x64 experiments through six-size ImageNet 512x512 evaluation, targeted robustness checks, and detailed adaptation code and resource reporting. It also clarifies evaluation repetition and adds an alternative feature-space metric. A material limitation remains: the broad superiority narrative insufficiently discusses Table 10, where guided teachers outperform the students on FDDINOv2. Nevertheless, the gains in empirical scope and reproducibility support a substantial overall improvement.
